target.title: Add Tailscale Serve support for WSL gateways
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Generated WSL gateways are loopback-only, so Companion cannot use a private tailnet endpoint.
- Why it matters: Users with Tailscale need secure remote access without LAN exposure, port forwarding, or localhost fallback.
- What changed: Added opt-in Tailscale Serve provisioning, browser/auth-key authorization, WSS gateway registration, Tailscale-aware recovery, runtime checks, redaction, and docs.
- User impact: New/replacement generated gateways can publish privately at `wss://<wsl-node>.<tailnet>.ts.net`; Tailscale identity authentication is trusted when enabled.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): No Funnel, Headscale, Tailscale SSH, subnet routing, named services, Windows Tailscale installation/removal, or in-place upgrades of existing gateways.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Docs / instructions
- [x] Tests / validation
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Tray / WinUI UX
- [ ] Windows node capability
- [ ] Local MCP / `winnode`
- [x] Gateway / connection / pairing
- [x] Setup / onboarding
- [x] Permissions / privacy / security
- [x] Tests / CI / docs

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #966 
- Related #TBD
- [ ] Related to a bug or regression

## Validation

- `.\build.ps1`
  - Passed: Shared, CLI, WinNode CLI, SetupEngine, and WinUI builds.
- `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests\OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests.csproj --no-restore`
  - Passed: 432, Failed: 0, Skipped: 0.
- `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Shared.Tests\OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore`
  - Passed: 2724, Failed: 0, Skipped: 31.
- `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore`
  - Passed: 1668, Failed: 0, Skipped: 0.
- `git diff --check`
  - Passed.

## Real behavior proof

- Environment tested: Windows host with authorized Tailscale and MagicDNS; generated `OpenClawGateway` WSL distro.
- PR head / commit tested: `12802b95 Add Tailscale Serve support for WSL gateways`
- Exact steps or command run:
  1. Replaced the existing generated WSL gateway through Companion setup with Tailscale Serve enabled.
  2. Authorized the generated WSL Tailscale node in the browser.
  3. Verified WSL status, Serve routing, Windows HTTPS reachability, Companion reconnect, and node invocation.
- Evidence after fix:
  - WSL Tailscale: `BackendState=Running`; `tailscaled` and `openclaw-gateway.service` active.
  - `tailscale serve status --json` reported HTTPS on port 443 proxying to `http://127.0.0.1:18789`.
  - Windows and WSL reported matching MagicDNS tailnets; Windows HTTPS request to the generated `.ts.net` endpoint returned HTTP 200.
  - Setup state: `TailscaleEnabled=true`, `IsLocalOnly=false`, WSS gateway URL.
  - Gateway registry: active app-managed local `wss://…ts.net` record with `SetupManagedDistroName=OpenClawGateway`.
  - Live policy verification: `gateway.auth.allowTailscale=true`, Serve active, and node invocation succeeded.
  - `openclaw nodes invoke --node "Windows Node (...)" --command device.info --params '{}'` returned `"ok": true`.
  - Setup log scan found zero `tskey-*` values and zero Tailscale authorization URLs.
- Observed result: Companion and its Windows node connected through the generated WSS Tailscale gateway; no localhost fallback was used.
- Screenshot/artifact links verified? N/A — live command output was used as the direct proof. An isolated setup run was also exercised; the existing-gateway replacement guard was not bypassed for a second visual pass.
- Not verified / blocked: No Funnel, Headscale, Tailscale SSH, subnet routing, or named Tailscale Services validation; these are intentionally out of scope.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes`)
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`)
- Data access scope changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation:
  - Tailscale-enabled gateways trust Tailscale identity authentication via `gateway.auth.allowTailscale=true`; tailnet ACLs therefore become an authorization control.
  - The feature is opt-in, requires an authorized Windows Tailscale client and matching MagicDNS tailnet, keeps OpenClaw loopback-bound inside WSL, and supports private Serve only—never Funnel.
  - Auth keys are transient, never accepted through CLI arguments or persisted config, and setup logs redact auth keys and Tailscale authorization URLs.
  - Device and token credentials remain available for pairing and compatibility.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`Yes`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)
- If yes, exact upgrade steps:
  - No migration is required. Existing gateways remain unchanged.
  - To opt in, create or replace an app-generated WSL gateway and enable **Tailnet access with Tailscale Serve**.
  - Optional headless inputs: `--tailscale`, `--tailscale-auth browser|auth-key`, `--tailscale-hostname`, and `OPENCLAW_SETUP_TAILSCALE_AUTH_KEY` for auth-key mode.

## Review Conversations

- [] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [] I left unresolved only conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

target.title: fix: stabilize OpenClaw beta setup and PT-PT formatting
target.body:
Related: #1000
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108435

## What Problem This Solves

The Windows Companion had two independent problems:

1. Compact numeric labels were culture-sensitive under `pt-PT` and other decimal-comma locales.
2. The Companion-owned setup path did not safely coordinate Gateway reload and restart behavior while the native OpenClaw wizard was running.

The Setup Engine also still defaulted to OpenClaw `2026.6.11`. This PR moves the supported default to the current stable release, `2026.7.1`, while keeping beta validation separate from the stable install path.

## Ownership and Design

- The Companion remains the owner of WSL, systemd, Gateway lifecycle, Windows Node bootstrap, and setup progress.
- OpenClaw remains the owner of the native onboarding wizard.
- The Companion uses the released, closed `wizard.start` schema and sends an empty parameter object. It does not require a custom OpenClaw protocol field or package.
- Gateway reload is suspended immediately before the first `wizard.start` and restored on success, failure, or cancellation.
- Restoration failure remains primary while preserving the original wizard exception or cancellation as inner evidence.
- The configured Gateway reload mode is restored, then the Gateway is explicitly restarted so wizard configuration is applied.
- Initial and reconnect wizard starts use the same schema-valid payload.

Official source readback confirms that both OpenClaw `v2026.7.1` and `v2026.7.2-beta.2` reject additional `wizard.start` properties. This PR therefore keeps the released contract rather than adding a Companion-side workaround.

## Changes

- Use invariant culture at the three existing compact-number formatting boundaries.
- Update the Setup Engine LKG from `2026.6.11` to stable `2026.7.1`.
- Move keepalive startup before pairing and wizard work.
- Suspend and restore `gateway.reload.mode` around the native wizard with fail-closed lifecycle handling.
- Reuse the current canonical WSL quoting helper.
- Include Windows Node bootstrap context in final setup progress.
- Align setup documentation with the real pipeline order.
- Add focused orchestration, cancellation, restoration, payload, and LKG tests.

## Validation

Validated on the current-main integration tree represented by this PR head:

- Setup Engine: `438/438` passed on the final public branch.
- Focused stable-version and wizard-schema tests: `4/4` passed.
- Full repository build and the Shared/Tray suites passed on the byte-identical reviewed integration tree before the no-force PR merge update.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Repo-native x64 dev installer built successfully.
- The installer completed with exit `0` in a disposable Windows Sandbox VM; installed product metadata was correct and the tray process remained running.
- MXC `wxc-exec --probe` selected `appcontainer-dacl`; a bounded allowed command passed, while a write outside the sole authorized root failed with `Access is denied` and created no file.
- Scoped `openclaw-autoreview` with Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` high: zero findings for the public branch; the final stable-target correction was `patch is correct` with confidence `0.97`.

Fresh GitHub CI on head `031c665b` installed official OpenClaw `2026.7.1` successfully in all three real WSL setup shards, then failed identically in `start-gateway`: the stable core retained its startup-migration lease beyond the Companion's 90-second health deadline, systemd reached its restart limit, and all later scenarios failed by cascade. This reproduces the linked OpenClaw P0 regression rather than a Companion compile, payload, or test failure.

OpenClaw `2026.7.2-beta.2` release notes include the core fix that releases this lease on startup exit, but beta remains a prerelease and is not silently substituted for the Companion's stable default here. The disposable Windows Sandbox image also does not expose nested virtualization, so it cannot replace the repository's real WSL2 setup proof. This PR remains draft pending an explicit release choice and green official-package E2E.

## Failed-First Evidence

- The first public review caught an unsupported `installDaemon` property in `wizard.start`. Current released schemas accept only their documented fields, so the payload was corrected to an empty object and tested.
- The first disposable-WSL run on the earlier integration line found a stale Gateway listener during restart preflight; fixture handling was corrected before the successful run.
- Review findings about suspension timing, reconnect payload parity, bootstrap progress, restoration coverage, and cancellation/restoration priority were accepted and fixed.
- A proposed extra restart caused only by restoring `gateway.reload.mode=restart` was rejected because OpenClaw documents `gateway.reload` as a reload exception. The Companion still performs its explicit post-wizard restart.

## Scope

- No `/new` or session behavior changes.
- No permission, token, secret, model, memory, plugin, agent-policy, or OpenClaw core changes.
- No custom OpenClaw package, protocol fork, or local-package transport is included.
- No operator runtime was installed or mutated for this validation; installer and MXC proof ran in the disposable Windows Sandbox lane.

## Security Impact

- New permissions or capabilities: No.
- Secret or token handling changes: No.
- New network destination: No.
- Broader command authority: No.

## Review Status

- [x] Rebased behavior integrated with current `main` without force-pushing the existing PR history.
- [x] Current stable and beta release metadata verified from official GitHub Releases and npm dist-tags.
- [x] Released `wizard.start` schemas verified for stable `2026.7.1` and beta `2026.7.2-beta.2`.
- [x] Current-head source, focused tests, full Setup Engine suite, and scoped Auto-review passed.
- [x] Companion installer and MXC allow/deny behavior proved in a disposable Windows VM.
- [ ] GitHub setup E2E passes against the selected official package. Current stable `2026.7.1` fails all three shards at its startup-migration lease; beta.2 contains the candidate core fix but is not the stable default.
- [ ] Maintainer review completed.

## Agent Transcript

<details>
<summary>Sanitized operator/agent decision record</summary>

- This work followed an extended operator/agent recovery and validation cycle rather than a quick version bump.
- The operator required the Companion and OpenClaw to remain separate products with explicit ownership: the Companion owns installation and service lifecycle; OpenClaw owns native onboarding.
- We rejected keeping a stale core indefinitely, shipping a beta as the stable default, and masking core lifecycle defects with sleeps, disabled E2E, or duplicated daemon ownership.
- Failed-first tests and review findings were preserved, triaged against current source and released schemas, fixed only when in scope, and rerun through repository tests, disposable Windows VM proof, MXC containment proof, and scoped Auto-review.
- The PR remains draft because its WSL2 setup layer still requires fresh repository E2E proof on the current head.

</details>

target.title: fix(setup): cancel node pairing cleanly instead of a spurious timeout warning + wasted retry
target.body:
Related: #1010

## What Problem This Solves

When a user cancels node setup while the pairing step is waiting to connect, the cancellation isn't handled cleanly: the step logs a misleading `"Node connection failed: Timeout"` warning (implying a connection problem, not a user abort), then **burns a retry** — `Task.Delay(3s, ct)` on the pairing step's retry policy — before the cancellation finally surfaces. The pipeline does end up `Cancelled` either way, but only after a spurious error and a wasted retry delay, and the journal/log record a connection "failure" that never happened.

## Why This Change Was Made

`WaitForNodeConnection` links the caller's token with an internal `CancelAfter(timeout)` and catches *every* `OperationCanceledException` as `NodeConnectionOutcome.Timeout`; `PairNodeStep.ExecuteAsync`'s catch-all then turns that into `StepResult.Fail(...)`. So a user cancel is reported as a failed connection attempt, which the step's retry policy (`MaxAttempts: 3`) then retries — and only the retry's `Task.Delay(..., ct)` tripping on the cancelled token gets the pipeline to `Cancelled`.

The fix makes the cancellation propagate directly, using the file's existing cancel-rethrow idiom (`SetupSteps.cs:1725`, `:2044`): guard the `Timeout` mapping with `when (!ct.IsCancellationRequested)`, and add `catch (OperationCanceledException) when (ct.IsCancellationRequested) { throw; }` ahead of `PairNodeStep`'s catch-all. The pipeline then maps the propagated OCE straight to `Cancelled` — no spurious "failed" log, no wasted retry. The genuine-timeout path is unchanged.

## Scope — what this does and doesn't change (traced end-to-end)

Being precise, because it's easy to overstate: **the final pipeline outcome is `Cancelled` (exit 3) with or without this change** — `PairNodeStep`'s retry policy means a caller-cancel trips the retry delay and surfaces as `Cancelled` regardless. What this PR changes is the *path* to that outcome on a user cancel:

- **Before:** `[Warn] Step 'pair-node' failed (attempt 1/3), retrying in 3s: Node connection failed: Timeout` → (retry delay) → `Cancelled`.
- **After:** cancellation surfaces immediately → `Cancelled`, no spurious warning, no retry delay.

So this is a cancellation-cleanliness / accurate-diagnostics fix, not an outcome change.

## User Impact

Cancelling node setup no longer emits a misleading "connection failed" warning to the log/journal or wastes a retry cycle — the abort is recorded and surfaced accurately and immediately. No change for a real connection timeout.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs or instructions
- [ ] Tests or validation
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore or infrastructure

## Scope

- [ ] Tray or WinUI UX
- [ ] Windows node capability
- [ ] Local MCP or `winnode`
- [ ] Gateway, connection, or pairing
- [x] Setup or onboarding
- [ ] Permissions, privacy, or security
- [ ] Tests, CI, or docs

## Validation

Full Windows CI-matrix mirror (win-x64, .NET 10.0.301), HEAD `294ef179` vs base `9fb1960e` — every project built and all 8 suites passed. Focused regression tests (both red on base, green on HEAD):

```
dotnet test tests/OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests \
  --filter "FullyQualifiedName~PairNodeStep_CallerCancellation|FullyQualifiedName~WaitForNodeConnection_CallerCancellation"
Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 2   (HEAD)
Failed! - Failed: 2, Passed: 0   (base, both fix hunks reverted)
```

These assert the code-level change: `WaitForNodeConnection` propagates the caller cancel instead of returning `Timeout`, and `PairNodeStep` rethrows it instead of swallowing it into `StepResult.Fail`.

(Two intermittent pre-existing flakes exist in the full matrix — `Connection.Tests.ConnectAndReconnect_EmitCompletedOperatorSpans` and `Tray.UITests.ChatTimelineVirtualizationProofTests` — on surfaces this SetupEngine-only diff doesn't touch; neither is a regression here.)

## Real Behavior Proof

Driving the **real** `SetupPipeline` through the real `PairNodeStep` with a caller cancel (loopback WebSocket that completes the upgrade then stays silent so the step parks in its wait; caller token cancelled 300 ms in), base vs HEAD:

- **base** (`9fb1960e`) — pipeline log:
  ```
  [Warn] Step 'pair-node' failed (attempt 1/3), retrying in 3s: Node connection failed: Timeout
  → SetupPipeline outcome: Cancelled (exit 3)
  ```
  i.e. a spurious connection-failure warning and a retry before it cancels.
- **HEAD** (`294ef179`) — pipeline log:
  ```
  → SetupPipeline outcome: Cancelled (exit 3)
  ```
  cancellation surfaces immediately; no "failed" warning, no retry.

Same final outcome; the fix removes the misleading warning and the wasted retry.

- Environment tested: Windows host, .NET SDK 10.0.301, win-x64
- PR head / base tested: `294ef179` / `9fb1960e`
- Screenshot or artifact links verified? `N/A` (non-UI setup/connection logic; proof is the paired pipeline-log capture + red→green tests)

## Security Impact

- New permissions or capabilities? `No`
- Secrets or tokens handling changed? `No`
- New or changed network calls? `No`
- Command or tool execution surface changed? `No`
- Data access scope changed? `No`

## Compatibility and Migration

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config or environment changes? `No`
- Migration needed? `No`

## Review History

Local review history (findings + dispositions per commit), including the correction from the original "reports Failed" framing to the accurate cancellation-cleanliness scope: https://gist.github.com/anagnorisis2peripeteia/0bdbede425c116811993f71fed9816b9
